title: Constructible integral modules in degree zero have perfect local models
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and selected uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, put $A=\operatorname{ULift}(R)$ and $I=(\operatorname{ULift}(\pi))\subseteq A$, and let $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/I^n)_X$ be the actual completed coefficient ring sheaf on the pro-étale site of $X$ [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients]. For every $B$-module sheaf $M$ with completed-constant stratified finitely presented local models [def-sfb-completed-constant-stratified], its degree-zero derived object $M[0]$ has stratified perfect coefficient models [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data]. The scalar modules in the local models may have torsion.

from.place: Proof, first sentence invoking sk-prop-integral-criterion: forward local-model argument in Proposition 6.8.11(3), resolving finitely presented valuation-ring modules by finite free modules.

proof.text: The chosen coefficient datum supplies a DVR. Transport its principal-ideal and domain properties along ULift. For a finite scalar module P choose a finite free surjection onto P. Its kernel is finite by Noetherianity and free because it is torsion-free over the PID. The distinguished triangle of this short exact sequence, rotated once, has P[0] as its middle object. The first object is finite free in degree zero and the third is the shift of another finite free module. The existing perfect triangle closure gives a bounded finite-projective model for P[0]. This is the two-term resolution argument, expressed through the already proved cone construction.

Keep the constructible finite strata, their scheme immersions, covering sieves and actual local module isomorphisms. Exact constant realization and completedConstantChange_exact carry the scalar derived isomorphism to an isomorphism from the degree-zero completed constant module to sfbCompletedModel. Exact inverse-image module pullback and slice restriction commute with singleFunctor. The actual representative-based sfbLocalRestriction is canonically isomorphic to the composite of those exact derived functors, so it transports this isomorphism. Compose it with the given local module isomorphism. The same scalar model, bounds and finite-projectivity witnesses establish stratified perfectness, including torsion modules and empty strata.

proof_origin.note: V4 formalizes the cited proof using existing exact-functor and perfect-triangle APIs; all new declarations are proved.

    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (M : proEtaleRingModules X
      (adicLisseCompletedRing X (ProEtale.IntegralConstantCompletion.ideal l E)))
    (hM : IsCompletedConstantStratified X
      (ProEtale.IntegralConstantCompletion.ideal l E) M) :
    IsSfbStratifiedPerfect X (ProEtale.IntegralConstantCompletion.ideal l E)
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)
